name: var_y
detail: bilinearity of Var with Cov(x,eps)=0; the thread's Var(y)=sigma^2 tau silently drops beta^2

name: corr_expression
detail: exact Corr = beta/sqrt(beta**2 + sigma**2*tau); thread = beta/(sigma*sqrt(tau)); equal only in the limit beta << sigma sqrt(tau)

name: corr_leading_order
claim: beta = rho sigma sqrt(tau) is right to O(rho^3)
detail: Corr(beta=rho sigma sqrt(tau)) = rho/sqrt(rho**2 + 1) = -rho**3/2 + rho + O(rho^5); relative error -rho^2/2

name: beta_inversion
detail: solving Corr(x,y)=rho for beta gives rho*sigma*sqrt(tau)*sqrt(-1/(rho - 1))/sqrt(rho + 1)

name: cost_bound
claim: kappa beta <= c  =>  rho <= c/(kappa sigma sqrt(tau))

name: exact_floor_residual
detail: solving rho/sqrt(1-rho^2) = a gives a/sqrt(a**2 + 1); bounded above by 1, so this reading never calls a horizon unreachable

name: floor_readings_agree_to_second_order
claim: the two readings of sigma agree to O(a^3)
detail: a/sqrt(1+a^2) = a - a^3/2 + O(a^5), so the readings differ only where the floor is a substantial fraction of 1

name: hedge_scaling
claim: double the cost and halve the vol => 4x the floor
detail: floor(2c, sigma/2)/floor(c, sigma) = 4; matches tweet 6/9 going 0.5% -> 2%

name: band_universality
claim: k = c/beta = kappa/m, free of sigma, tau and c
detail: k = kappa/m; so trade frequency and gross capture are functions of the multiple alone

name: trunc_first_moment
detail: integral evaluates to k*erf(sqrt(2)*k/2) - k + sqrt(2)*exp(-k**2/2)/sqrt(pi)

name: trunc_second_moment
detail: integral evaluates to -k**2*erf(sqrt(2)*k/2) + k**2 - sqrt(2)*k*exp(-k**2/2)/sqrt(pi) - erf(sqrt(2)*k/2) + 1

name: trunc_moment_limits
claim: k->0 gives E|x| = sqrt(2/pi) and E[x^2] = 1

name: proportional_sharpe
claim: per-period Sharpe of h=x is rho/sqrt(1+rho^2) ~ rho
detail: SR = rho/sqrt(1+rho^2); equals rho to O(rho^3), so IC is the per-bet Sharpe to leading order and IR = IC sqrt(BR) follows as an approximation, given independence across bets

name: proportional_sharpe_loading_form
claim: with r = beta/(sigma sqrt(tau)), SR = r/sqrt(1+2 r^2)
detail: the same Sharpe through the loading-to-noise ratio; equals the rho form under r = rho/sqrt(1-rho^2), and differs from it otherwise

name: r2_ir_bridge_is_approximate
claim: exact IR^2/BR = R^2/(1+R^2), so R^2 = IR^2/BR holds only to O(rho^4)
detail: IR^2/BR is the per-bet squared Sharpe rho^2/(1+rho^2); reading it as R^2 = rho^2 is the small-IC limit

name: effective_breadth
detail: BR_eff = n/(rho_a*(n - 1) + 1); -> 1/rho_alpha as N -> infinity, so alpha crowding caps breadth however many names are added
